builds.name: Reference: Attack-led side lane
builds.goal: Reference for Viego: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A melee reset fighter who seeks a first takedown, uses mist for approach and temporarily adopts a fallen enemy's tools. Measure getting the first takedown with Viego's own kit before possession. Borrowed abilities/items during possession cannot be mixed with all his original attacks as permanent DPS. Real attacks can exploit BotRK and Spellblade while Hullbreaker asks for side-lane pressure.
builds.summary: Real attacks can exploit BotRK and Spellblade while Hullbreaker asks for side-lane pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Viego: Measure getting the first takedown with Viego's own kit before possession. Borrowed abilities/items during possession cannot be mixed with all his original attacks as permanent DPS.

Start with the early core (BotRK or Trinity, then the other) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Real attacks can exploit BotRK and Spellblade while Hullbreaker asks for side-lane pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Viego's spectral blade passively deals bonus percent current Health damage On-Hit and strikes twice vs. enemies he recently hit with an Ability, stealing Health.

builds.name: Mist AP second hit
builds.summary: Test AP supporting mist access, W control and ability-marked follow-up attacks.
builds.goal: Test AP supporting mist access, W control and ability-marked follow-up attacks.
builds.hypothesis: W has 1 AP magic damage, E's movement speed scales with AP and Q's marked second attack includes 0.15 AP physical damage plus a heal. Nashor and Dusk support direct attacks during mist, while AP also enters possession healing. The first possession replaces Viego's current items with the victim's items.
testPlan: Required state: Ability mark present, mist contact and target attackable; test pre-possession first.
Separate W, first attack, Q follow-up and healing with AP varied; repeat before and during a specified possession.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Low AD weakens normal Q/R threat and possession interrupts the planned item budget.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Viego's six owned items are not continuously retained during possession.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Riftmaker, Cosmic Drive, Rabadon's Deathcap, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Heartbreaker crit window

builds.goal: Test source-explicit crit-stat scaling on Q and R before cashing an ultimate attack volley.
builds.hypothesis: Q and R expose distinct crit-stat multiplier expressions; R also adds missing-health physical damage. Fiendhunter grants enhanced basic attacks after ultimate use and E supplies attack speed. Infinity Edge/Collector emphasize the opening, with armor penetration supporting confirmed physical packets.
testPlan: Required state: R ready, specified crit stats, target health recorded and no possession item replacement during baseline.
Vary crit chance/damage independently and log Q/R packets plus three post-R basic attacks.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: R targets a different lowest-percent-health champion or the burst fails to secure the next soul.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: A crit-stat multiplier does not prove Q/R randomly crit or duplicate every attack effect.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
